ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including Articles 3-2 and 3-3); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on RBE filing forms; amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, governing SCSp formation; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02, as amended, on AML/CFT obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / extract from foreign trade registry of the sole general partner or corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for issuers not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the general partner or corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign trade registry or ministry of justice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy of each beneficial owner, general partner, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true-copy certificate plus Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each beneficial owner and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of each individual beneficial owner and controlling corporate shareholder
Criminal record extract or equivalent certificate of conduct for any natural-person general partner and proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National judicial records authority in the person's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) screening under the Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF standards. The Luxembourg notary, incorporating party, and any regulated professional support service provider must screen every UBO, director, and general partner against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions implemented in Luxembourg, OFAC SDN List for USD payment rails, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs frozen assets list. Screening is required before incorporation and continuously thereafter. Any positive PEP or sanctions match triggers senior-management approval, enhanced due diligence, and immediate reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) where required by law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes / Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be written in Latin alphabet characters; names originally in Cyrillic, Greek, CJK, or other non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into French, German, or Luxembourgish Romanized form. The legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or the full wording 'Société en commandite spéciale' is mandatory. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names, must not be contrary to public order or morality, and must not mislead the public about the purpose or legal form of the undertaking.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société Nationale de Crédit et d'Investissement
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or notary may file a written administrative challenge (recours gracieux) with the Registrar within 15 days of the rejection notice, supplying evidence of distinguishability and requested amendments. If the challenge is unsuccessful or not resolved, a judicial appeal may be brought before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg with the assistance of a Luxembourg-qualified lawyer. A one-time renewal of a valid name reservation may be requested for an additional 30 days before expiry; after expiry a new reservation and clearance application must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only when provided by a Luxembourg-regulated professional support service provider or trust company under a written registered-office agreement, with full statutory mail-handling and access to records in Luxembourg. For an ISIC 5813 digital magazine portal with no physical cash operations, the business-model risk of a virtual office is low, but the general partner and any Luxembourg-based substance agent must maintain real operational substance or be able to demonstrate adequate substance under Luxembourg tax and CRS rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximate annual probability of less than 5% in the absence of tax, AML, or reputational red flags. For a purely digital publishing and sponsored media business, Luxembourg tax and AML authorities are more likely to request documentary substance and financial-flow evidence than to conduct an unannounced physical on-site inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and 30-day reservation at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative tariff per search and reservation voucher

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized true-copy certification, apostille/consular legalization, and sworn translation of foreign UBO corporate and identity documents into French or German
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities, Luxembourg consulate or diplomatic delegation, and sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff based on number of documents and pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notarial preparation of the SCSp partnership deed and RCS initial filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary and Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and RCS administrative filing schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
PEP and sanctions database screening of each UBO, general partner, and authorized signatory using commercial KYC data and sanctions lookup
Registered office agreement with Luxembourg professional support/trust services provider for the first year
Luxembourg legal counsel pre-incorporation due diligence review, name compatibility check, and legal opinion on SCSp formation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing hourly or matter-based fee for a compact pre-incorporation engagement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (particularly Articles 317-1 to 317-21 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale by the Law of 12 July 2013); complementary provisions of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on the accounting and annual accounts of undertakings, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating the MyLBR electronic filing portal in coordination with the Caisse de consignation (Repository) for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statutory declaration of deposit (déclaration de dépôt) attaching the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société / partnership agreement) filed electronically via the MyLBR portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; capital contribution is freely fixed in the partnership agreement and may be in cash or in kind. No legal escrow or deposit duty applies to unregulated SCSp vehicles; any subscribed capital must be paid or promised as contractually agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the partnership agreement of [NAME] SCSp, constituted under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, be and is hereby approved and adopted, and each subscribing partner accepts the partnership interests allocated in Schedule I; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name(s)] be and is/are hereby appointed as manager(s) (gérant(s)) with full authority to represent the SCSp, open bank accounts, execute digital publishing and advertising contracts, and instruct professional advisors; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the manager(s) shall file this resolution with the Luxembourg Business Registers, obtain the RCS registration number, register beneficial owners in the RBE, and complete all statutory ancillary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name verification and registered office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online pre-selection via lbr.lu and local municipal office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search in the RCS index; submit a name reservation request through MyLBR where applicable; obtain written consent of the owner of the proposed registered office premises confirming address availability for registration purposes and for receipt of official notices.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form (MyLBR)
Copy of the proposed registered office lease or landlord consent letter
Proof of identity of signatories (passport copies)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or prejudges third-party rights, submit three alternative names with corrected filing; obtain a formal negative attestation from LBR and re-file for a distinct name; judicial recourse lies before the Tribunal de l'arrondissement within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, signature and notarization of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) or lawyer if using a private deed with legalized signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalize the partnership agreement containing mandatory particulars enumerated in Article 317-1 et seq. of the 1915 Law: name, registered office, purpose, identity of general and limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing rules, management powers, and audit rights. Execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary in notarial form (recommended for legal certainty) or as private writing with signatures legalized by the competent authority; ensure each subscriber initializes the subscription schedule.
required_dossiers: Approved partnership agreement (final draft)
Schedule of partners with full names, addresses, nationalities and contribution amounts
Passport copies and proof of residential address of all partners
Bank reference or proof of in-kind contribution valuation
Proposed registered office lease
Draft power of attorney if a signatory is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or legalization office identifies discrepancies, the deed is corrected by way of an addendum or re-executed identical deed; missing signatures are cured by supplementary signature under the supervising notary's control; any defective contribution valuation is cured by a revised schedule approved by all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the RCS and issuance of the registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via MyLBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed deed, the statutory declaration of deposit, proof of fee payment and all supporting annexes to MyLBR; select regime code for SCSp (11G or applicable); request issuance of the RCS identification number and the certificate of registration. The registry checks formal legal conformity and, upon approval, publishes a registration notice.
required_dossiers: Executed notarial deed or private deed with legalized signatures
Filing declaration signed by a manager or authorized agent
Confirmation of registered office address with landlord consent
Identification documents of all article signatories
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Payment confirmation of the RCS fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a query or issues a notice of insufficiency, respond within the stated cure period (typically 8-15 days) by submitting supplemental particulars; if registration is refused, file an appeal with the district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within one month; alternatively, correct the deed and promptly re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and procurement of the LEI code
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA repository and Legal Entity Identifier issuing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the registry transmits the filing particulars for publication in the RESA (electronic compendium of companies and associations); concurrently file a separate application with the LBR, acting as an LEI Local Operating Unit, to obtain the Legal Entity Identifier for the SCSp using the RCS registration number and proof of corporate existence.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
LEI application form (LBR form)
Partnership agreement extract confirming legal structure
Official corporate details: exact entity name, legal form 'Société en Commandite Spéciale', registered office, RCS number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or inaccurate, contact the LBR helpdesk for correction order; if LEI issuance is refused, verify consistency of corporate details with RCS data and re-submit corrected records; any LEI lapse is remedied by re-application with updated annual renewal data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership declaration (RBE) and supplementary tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of registration, file the RBE declaration identifying all ultimate beneficial owners with exact percentage of ownership or control; separately register the SCSp for VAT purposes with the AEDT using the RCS number and EU VAT number application form where the digital magazine portal will perform taxable supplies (advertising, subscriptions); obtain a Luxembourg VAT ID.
required_dossiers: RBE filing form with full names, dates of birth and nationalities of beneficial owners
Ownership/control schedule of the SCSp
VAT registration form (form 645)
Certificate of commencement of activity (attestation de début d'activité)
Copy of the partnership agreement and RCS certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or erroneous RBE declaration attracts graduated fines and registered defaults; cure by immediate corrected filing plus formal explanation to the RBE office; VAT registration objections are remedied by completing the AEDT questionnaire and providing supplementary evidence of taxable supplies; an appeal against AEDT decisions is available to the Director of the Administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of bank/institutional account and payment processor onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or licensed PFS/e-money institution; independent onboarding with Stripe and Google AdSense
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a professional corporate bank account (e.g., in a Luxembourg bank or a supervised PFS) presenting the RCS certificate, partnership agreement, RBE proof and beneficial owner identification; complete know-your-customer documentation. Thereafter, activate payment rails: create the Stripe merchant account under the SCSp's legal identity, verify UBO documentation and website ownership; register the digital magazine portal with Google AdSense/Ad Manager using the LEI and VAT number, submitting traffic and content-compliance disclosures.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration (less than 3 months old)
Partnership agreement and LEI certificate
RBE registration confirmation
Passport copies and proof of residence of all beneficial owners
Banking references and source of funds declarations
Domain ownership proof and privacy policy of the digital magazine portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines onboarding on AML grounds, submit complete source-of-funds documentation or apply to an alternative Luxembourg supervised institution; if Stripe or AdSense refuses settlement, correct merchant category codes (MCC 5111/5192 compatible digital media) and provide signed business description; appeal the processor decision through their dispute channel or migrate to an alternate acquiring processor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate General for SMEs and Middle Classes, in administrative coordination with the municipal business premises office; no sectoral license applies to pure digital publishing under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement) – prima facie not required for the purely digital editorial and sponsored-media activity; a local municipal premises permit may be voluntarily requested if the entity maintains a physical office address open to the public or performs on-site production activities (printing, warehousing)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt category – digital magazine production and office-based activities do not appear in the annexes requiring a full EIA or environmental permit; only a simplified waste registration may be recommended for professional premises generating office waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges expected; compliance with general municipal wastewater and household waste thresholds; electronic waste subject to Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE) and Luxembourg implementing waste regulations; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions not applicable in the absence of printing, coating, or chemical processes; server-hosting emissions are addressed contractually through green hosting and energy-efficiency undertakings

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) obtainable from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) for premises with public access or mixed-use occupancy; structural load inspection to be performed by a registered engineer where server rooms or storage mezzanines are installed; workplace abandonment clearance and work-station compliance (ergonomics, lighting, emergency exits) under Articles L.311-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Labor Code, administered by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and excise registration; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income tax competencies; consolidated digital portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign SCSp must appoint an established Luxembourg tax representative (assujetti) with an approved establishment, obtain a national business identification number (matricule) from the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), and file VAT registration with the AEDT on Form 640a indicating the appointed representative. Non-established taxable persons are denied the domestic EUR 35,000 small-business waiver and must register from the first euro, while an established SCSp follows the standard RCS-plus-AEDT workflow.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent per the Luxembourg law of 12 July 2013; it is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at entity level. No check-the-box or opt-in corporate-taxation election is available under Luxembourg law; partners are taxed directly on their distributive shares, subject to ATAD anti-hybrid and, where applicable, reverse-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 10,000 (EU-wide annual turnover threshold for intra-Community B2C supplies of electronically supplied services and distance sales; above this, OSS registration or local Luxembourg VAT registration is required). Non-established suppliers have no de minimis relief and register from the first euro; domestically established taxable persons may use the EUR 35,000 small-business exemption only for purely domestic B2C supplies outside the digital-services OSS regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg operates no real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) system; e-invoicing is permitted using Factur-X / ZUGFeRD / EDI formats, and B2G e-invoicing through the PEPPOL network is mandatory for public contracts. There is no API-based stamping or digital VAT-clearance requirement for digital magazine publishing services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: B2C supplies of electronically supplied services to non-EU customers are placed outside Luxembourg VAT scope under place-of-supply rules and are effectively 0% without invoking the refund mechanism; B2B supplies to non-EU customers qualify for zero-rating subject to proof of the customer's non-EU VAT/economic-operator status; physical export of tangible media qualifies for 0% VAT only if dispatch or transport out of the EU is evidenced within 90 days of the supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT's automated risk-scoring engine reconciles export declarations, payment timing, and zero-rating evidence in the e-TVA data warehouse. Unsustainable zero-rating claims trigger immediate VAT reassessment with retroactive clawback of input VAT deducted on attributable costs, default interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum), and administrative fines up to EUR 500,000; fraudulent export schemes additionally expose the SCSp and its representatives to criminal penalties of up to 10 years' imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating as the national central bank of Luxembourg within the Eurosystem and under the ultimate monetary authority of the European Central Bank (ECB). Prudential and AML/CFT supervision over credit institutions and payment institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies. Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control regime and imposes no restriction on current-account or capital-account operations; such freedom is guaranteed by Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Capital contributions to, and profit remittances from, an SCSp may be freely routed in EUR or in any foreign currency. A Luxembourg-resident SCSp is fiscally transparent, and distributions to non-resident limited partners carry no Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, so the principal remittance hurdle does not arise. The residual constraints are limited to OECD transfer-pricing documentation for intra-group disbursements and to the risk of Luxembourg permanent-establishment attribution where a fully liable general partner performs management functions in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the Eurozone impose no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio; the SCSp may retain 100% of foreign-currency export or service receipts indefinitely. The only reporting analogue is the duty of the receiving credit institution to report cross-border transactions of EUR 12,500 or above to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics; that obligation is statistical in nature and has no repatriation or conversion consequence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. EU-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, Revolut Business and comparable PSD2 firms may passport into Luxembourg with only a CSSF notification and can efficiently collect multi-currency Stripe and AdSense payouts. However, an SCSp's lack of legal personality creates UBO-mapping and signatory-authority complexity, and several EMIs decline partnership-type entities that have no corporate body. An EMI cannot substitute for a Luxembourg credit institution for capital-commitment escrow, statutory audit comfort letters, intra-group lending, or interest-bearing treasury balances beyond the narrow E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC perimeter.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Luxembourg statutory rule mandates physical appearance; CSSF Circular 20/744 and Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS) permit remote video-identification and electronic signature for onboarding. In practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one teleconference or physical interview with the general partner (gérant) and each authorised signatory, and a physical closing is commonly imposed when the general partner is a non-EEA entity or where the partnership agreement contains discretionary carried-interest or profit-waterfall clauses that complicate UBO attribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp without legal personality: the bank must anchor signature authority, economic-ownership mapping and account-control rules in the partnership contract, creating a perceived governance and accounting-capacity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or notarised special limited partnership agreement identifying the general partner and all limited partners, the capital-account schedule, profit-sharing ratios and every UBO interest exceeding 25%; an extract from the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) if the SCSp is registered; a formal resolution of the general partner appointing the account signatories with specimen signatures; and a structural note demonstrating that the SCSp may lawfully hold bank accounts and acquire rights and obligations in its own name under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate ownership and US/EEA platform revenue (AdSense, Stripe) trigger CRS classification, FATCA reporting-status checks and source-of-wealth scrutiny for each beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS self-certification and FATCA forms (W-8IMY for the fiscally transparent partnership and W-8BEN-E for each corporate limited partner) maintained current at the bank; a Luxembourg fiscal-residency attestation (form 210) or a treaty-based tax-transparency opinion confirming that the SCSp is transparent and non-resident for corporate income tax; signed source-of-wealth statements and passport copies for each individual UBO behind any capital contribution exceeding EUR 250,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Merchant-payout flows from Stripe and Google AdSense may resemble settlement-agent activity or invoicing round-tripping if the SCSp cannot evidence its publishing operations and the corresponding commercial contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform agreements with Stripe and Google Ireland Limited recorded in the name of the SCSp; publisher contracts for ad slots, sponsorship placements and magazine subscriptions evidencing the ISIC 5813 commercial model; a twelve-month payout history cross-referenced to editorial deliverables; domain ownership certificates, content-licence agreements and hosting invoices substantiating genuine digital magazine operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VAT and e-publication classification: sponsorship income constitutes B2B advertising services while subscriptions constitute B2C electronic publication supplies, and the bank may demand confirmation of the applicable VAT treatment before validating the payment rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg VAT registration certificate (numéro d'identification à la TVA) where the SCSp makes taxable supplies; a tax desk opinion confirming the reduced VAT rate for e-magazine publications and the place-of-supply rules for sponsorship income; standard contractual templates that separate subscription revenue, advertisement revenue and sponsored-media placements, thereby providing an unbroken audit trail from the PSP settlement to the SCSp accounting records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions must be routed by wire only, never by cash or third-party sweep. EEA investors use Target2/SEPA credit transfers to the SCSp LU-format IBAN; non-EEA investors use SWIFT MT103 with a concise field-70 narrative identifying the payer, the SCSp name and the reference of the partnership agreement, and the BPM6 purpose code for direct investment in equity capital. The receiving Luxembourg bank automatically reports cross-border credits of EUR 12,500 or above to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics; for amounts above EUR 250,000 a funds-origin declaration and a signed capital-call instruction from the general partner must accompany the transfer. The capital-account ledger maintained by the general partner serves as the controlling evidentiary record for audit, CRS and UBO purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR operating payments are cleared through SEPA Credit Transfer, including SEPA Instant where same-day settlement is contractually required. Non-EUR disbursements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 over the bank's correspondent network, including CHIPS or Fedwire for USD. Commercial documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) may be issued for large supplier contracts, though digital magazine counterparties are normally settled on open account. Profit distributions to non-resident limited partners are executed as SWIFT MT103 transfers with a direct-investor distribution purpose code, accompanied by a signed distribution resolution, a current partners-capital table and CRS-compliant jurisdiction data; no Luxembourg withholding tax applies to the fiscally transparent SCSp distribution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards concluded under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank-standard FX terms with a CSSF-licensed credit institution, used to hedge forecasted advertising revenue and licensing fees.
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps for long-term balance-sheet hedging of USD-denominated commercial debt or payables, subject to partnership-agreement authorisation and OECD transfer-pricing compliance.
Vanilla EUR/USD FX options acquired on a purchased-only basis for downside protection on multi-currency cash positions, with premium payments treated as treasury expenses.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible in principle under EU EMIR but practically unnecessary for the eurozone since EUR/USD is a fully deliverable market; relevant only if the SCSp collects revenue in a restricted convertible currency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year entity, by 31 July N+1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial court injunction order with pecuniary penalty up to EUR 10,000; failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years triggers managed strike-off from RCS, public notice of default, and joint and several civil liability of the gérants

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) check and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any change in partnership interests above 10% or change in material control; no recurring annual filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years for wilful omission, false declaration, or refusal to disclose beneficial ownership information

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies if the SCSp fails the small undertaking exemption and exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, and >50 employees on average during the financial year
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under Law of 19 December 2002 as amended; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted where elected

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO filing exists for an SCSp; the entity must maintain a register of beneficial owners at the registered office and report changes to the RBE within 30 days. The annual register audit must verify the partner list, allocation of partnership interests, control rights, and UBO identification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,500-3,500 EUR p.a. (approx. 1,700-3,900 USD) for registered office and domiciliation in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000-12,000 EUR p.a. (approx. 4,500-13,400 USD) for statutory audit of a small to mid-size publishing entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% of CIT, and municipal business tax ~6.75% in Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for new tangible assets), notional interest deduction (NID) on equity increases

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) for the SCSp as a transparent entity; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (ACD) e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted (typically up to 6 months).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp (name, RCS number, address, fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the SCSp's Luxembourg RCS number and local address; non-resident partners must be identified with their tax residence and foreign tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide income (revenue, gains, and other income) before deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all income attributable to the SCSp's activities, including digital advertising and subscription revenue, regardless of partner residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (operating costs, royalties, interest, depreciation, and amortization)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically connected to the SCSp's income are deductible; ensure arm's length pricing for cross-border payments to related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (Box 2 minus Box 3) before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply any available loss carryforward (indefinite) subject to anti-abuse rules; non-resident partners must report their share in their own tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income to partners (pro rata based on partnership agreement)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide each partner's share of income, name, address, and tax identification number; non-resident partners are taxed in Luxembourg only on Luxembourg-source income unless treaty relief applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from €50 to €5,000 per month, plus interest of 0.5% per month on unpaid tax; deliberate non-filing may lead to criminal prosecution and fines up to €250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the SCSp holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 12 months; treaty rates may apply for non-EU residents)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a Luxembourg tax residency certificate (TRC) and submit a formal request (Form 22) to the Luxembourg tax administration before the distribution date. The reduced rate is applied only after approval; otherwise, the statutory rate is withheld and a refund claim must be filed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive (if beneficial owner is an EU associated company). Interest: statutory 15%, reduced to 0% under the same directive. Treaty rates may further reduce these rates (e.g., 5% for royalties under many DTAs).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group turnover for Master File; EUR 1 million for Local File (for intercompany transactions exceeding this threshold). The SCSp must prepare documentation if it engages in controlled transactions with related parties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The SCSp must demonstrate economic substance in Luxembourg if it claims treaty benefits or engages in cross-border financing/royalty flows. Requirements include a local office, qualified staff, board meetings in Luxembourg, and substantive decision-making. Failure to meet substance may lead to denial of treaty benefits and reclassification of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of digital advertising revenue or subscription income, or artificial shifting of profits to low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties of 10% to 50% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pass-through entity without any physical presence, employees, or business activity in Luxembourg, while claiming treaty benefits or engaging in intra-group transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of income, and imposition of a 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions; administrative fines up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for the company's tax debts if they fail to ensure substance; travel bans may be issued in cross-border investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence on advertisers or subscribers, or processing payments through opaque channels without proper KYC/AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for the entity; criminal liability for responsible officers; suspension of operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines up to €500,000 for AML violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for digital content licensing or advertising services that deviate from arm's length, without adequate documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties of 10% to 50% of the additional tax, and interest on underpayments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they signed inaccurate TP documentation; criminal charges for fraud in severe cases.
